💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as people have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.
  • Sources indicate that this fresh option arrived fairly quietly as part of an revision that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup.
  • Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as people have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

Sources indicate that this fresh option arrived fairly quietly as part of an revision that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a big deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the new patch, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

According to recent reports, "Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," indicates one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

Sources indicate that in order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Recent findings suggest that not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" says another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

According to recent reports, the release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, stated on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon.".

In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead promptly.

But then things began moving promptly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

Industry observers note that later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a upcoming name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history.".

The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will enhancement if I receive a reply.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside Fresh York where we could imagine our future children growing up.
  • It looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale.
  • Industry observers note that our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside Fresh York where we could imagine our future children growing up. We looked upstate, in Connecticut, and at all those charming hamlets strung along the eastern end of Long Island known as the Hamptons. Toured hundreds of houses, clicked thousands of listings. But not one felt like home.

Nevins in her garden in East Hampton.

It looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale. A great furrowed trunk rising from a froth of flowering vines that split into enormous limbs sweeping improbably far across the garden. Its arrangement was so baroque—veiny, muscular wood twisting and reaching, dissolving overhead into a canopy of green delicacy. We could picture our children climbing its winding branches, little hands against its ridged, mossy bark.

Industry observers note that our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend. Now we joke that we didn’t buy a house—we bought this tree.

But what is it? A butternut tree? An oak? A black walnut? Deborah Nevins, one of the most revered living landscape designers, created this garden for the previous owners in 2004. In the fall, she invited me to her white-shingled cottage in Springs, East Hampton, to find out. Her living room has triple-hung windows like those in Monticello, Thomas Jefferson’s house in Virginia, which go down to the floor so it’s easy to wheel in her potted lemon trees when the seasons change. “Winter is divine; it’s when they bloom,” she coos. “The house smells of lemon blossoms.”.

David Geffen’s pool at his former Beverly Hills estate, once home to Warner Bros.’ Jack Warner.

“Butternut!” she declares, slamming the book shut with all the force of her petite five-foot-nothing frame. “For sure.”.

This is our tree. A butternut that likely sprouted generations before she came along. “It’s a native tree, probably a hundred years old. But I’d have to know the caliper—the diameter about a foot up—to be more precise.” She decided it’d be the anchor for our yard design the moment she saw it—existing mature trees are “sacred” and must be preserved at all costs. At its base, she dared to plant clematis, usually a climbing vine, that now rambles across the ground, softening the old tree’s trunk with a tangle of flowers. The butternut divides the rest of the property into distinct passages, including an ornamental reflecting pool bordered by hornbeam hedges, a lap pool shaded under locust trees, and a gravel path lined with rounded boxwoods.

GREEK MYTHOLOGY It took Nevins eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete her collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. What was once a parking lot is now planted with more than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs.

A rendering of the 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens.

To Nevins, the tree is an excellent example of her greater gardening philosophy: “I’m interested in creating unfolding spaces which intensify [the viewers’] experience, your sense of place and movement through a garden,” she claims. She frequently builds hedges and allées to control viewers’ attention, like horse blinders. “Not every aspect of the garden is seen at once. You have to stop and think.”.

Sources indicate that over the last four decades, Nevins has been entrusted with the grounds of some extraordinary spaces. Her clients include media mogul David Geffen, fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger, former Disney chairman Michael Eisner, and hotelier Ian Schrager. Commissions can range from tiny residential spaces (like mine) to huge commercial projects abroad. It took her eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete a 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens. That was a collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on a landscape that climbs over the buildings themselves, planted with native grasses from the hills of Attica and fragrant Mediterranean herbs, including lavender, rosemary, and oregano. Nevins’s mantra for the project was simple: “Speak Greek.” The execution was anything but simple. More than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs fill the public work. Nevins conceptualized the totality of the park. “I chose every single tree!” she states. “We had to propagate hundreds of thousands of plants throughout Greece, and we decided to hire various nurseries so that if there was a disease or fire, the entire crop would not be wiped out.” Her effort impressed Piano. “It is always special when, beyond the work on a project itself, you realize that you share the same values and ideas,” says Piano of Nevins, whom he describes as a “wonderful professional and human adventure.”.

“There is discipline in her work but never rigidity,” says Scott Mitchell, the West Coast–based architect who met Nevins at a dinner honoring architect Richard Meier in 1997 and went on to work with her on properties for Geffen in both California and Upcoming York. “Her landscapes don’t compete with architecture; they give it a place to belong.”.

Sources indicate that he recalls the “emotional power” of her work for Geffen at the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, former home of Warner Bros. cofounder Jack Warner. “Endless sweeps of white azaleas, a driveway lined with ancient, gnarled native sycamores, and 11 acres of rolling meadow beneath giant coast live oaks,” Mitchell states. “World-class projects require cohesion between architecture and landscape. They have to play from the same sheet of music. Debby totally gets that. Her response to architecture is clear and harmonious—confident but never overstepping.”.

Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo at their Mustique estate.

In a recent development, gil Schafer, a Upcoming York–based architect who has worked with Nevins on more than 25 houses and gardens, also commends her command of structure. At his own house near Millbrook, she built a 12-foot-high hornbeam enclosure nestled into the surrounding farm fields that has, he claims, “an almost abstract sculptural quality—as if Richard Serra had suddenly decided to work in hornbeam rather than Corten steel.”.

Nevins was born in Manhattan at what was then the Doctors Hospital on the Upper East Side. The family resided in the penthouse of the same building where Greta Garbo lived. Her father died of a brain tumor at 43, when Nevins was six months old, and so her mother had to return to work. At six, she was sent to Camp Taconic in Massachusetts. “I was tiny! My mother might have been arrested today.” She remembers walking in the woods, finding a strawberry, and reporting the discovery in a letter home. The seed had been planted—pun quite obvious.

Fleur Cowles, the formidable editor behind the short-lived, extravagantly inventive magazine Flair, was a maternal relative and had an outsize impact on her childhood. “She knew everyone, and she was so brilliant,” Nevins states, offering me an issue of Flair from another bookshelf like a cherished family heirloom. Another influence was her mother’s sister, Miriam Sampson, an interior decorator who lived across from Carnegie Hall. “In this massive apartment, she had her office in one room, and she had little models of apartments. I was so intrigued,” Nevins recalls. She’d cut out pictures of interiors and gardens from magazines and assemble them in scrapbooks. “But I didn’t even know about this idea of being a landscape architect.”.

In a recent development, when Nevins was 14, her mother remarried and the family moved to Upcoming Haven, Connecticut. She went on to attend Boston University for undergrad and returned to New York for graduate school at Columbia. “They didn’t think that landscape history, which is what I wanted to study, was academic enough. And they probably had no one to teach it anyway,” she notes. So she earned an MA and an MPhil in art history. Travel became a form of individualized study. “I learned by looking,” she says. She sought out Le Corbusier’s buildings in France, including La Tourette, Maisons Jaoul, and Villa Savoye, and drove from Paris to Santiago de Compostela looking at Romanesque and Merovingian churches. She made her first of many pilgrimages to Sissinghurst, a garden in Kent created by the writer Vita Sackville-West and her diplomat husband, Harold Nicolson. “There’s nothing more beautiful than Sissinghurst,” she sighs.

One of Nevins’s greatest champions has been Geffen, whom Victoria Newhouse, the renowned architecture critic and widow of longtime Condé Nast chairman Si Newhouse, introduced her to. On her first meeting with Geffen, Nevins arrived to present her work with a carousel of 80 slides. “After maybe 30 slides, he states, ‘That’s enough. You’re hired.’ And I thought to myself, Who is this guy?” When she looked him up, she read that one of his attributes is spotting talent. “And that was that.”.

At the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, she removed one swimming pool to open up the landscape, built a new one with a new patio house where Warner had a putting green, and relocated several mature oak trees on the property. “David is not afraid of big moves,” she notes. (They preserved the fountains and terraces Warner had commissioned from Florence Yoch, who designed the grounds of Tara for Gone With the Wind, of course.) However, according to Nevins, when Warner’s daughter came to see what Geffen had done, she looked around and asked if they had changed anything. “ ‘What did we change? We changed everything!’ ” Nevins remembers Geffen saying. “The idea that we didn’t do a thing is crazy, but that it looked like it was meant to be—that’s a good thing. The ultimate compliment that looks like I did nothing.”.

An aerial view of Deborah Nevins’s Hamptons garden.

Hilfiger hired Nevins for a property in Mustique in the early 1990s, and again for his Denbigh Farm in Greenwich in 1995. In the Caribbean, she created palm promenades and a courtyard of white flowers; in Connecticut, she brought the elements of an old estate into a coherent whole. “I knew she was incredibly passionate about her work, and that always interested me because I love working with people who are passionate about what they do,” Hilfiger says. “Her execution was impeccable, and she delivered exactly what she promised.”.

Nevins’s office is based in Fresh York City, and she keeps between 5 and 10 new projects going at all times. “Almost any job is interesting unless I hear in advance that the people aren’t nice,” she says. “Also, art collectors, in my experience, have been great patrons. If you’re an art collector—and you’re truly not collecting just to make money from art—you have an interest in beauty and understanding.”.

PLEACHY KEEN “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say,” architect Gil Schafer notes of Nevins. “She feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

Industry observers note that on average, it takes two years to get a garden up and running, three years if she needs to build new structures. But a garden is never finished. Roberta Denning, who with her husband, Steve, commissioned Nevins for her family’s property in Greenwich in 2006, describes the pleasure of living with something that acquires depth while continuing to change. “What she created has grown more valuable with time,” Denning notes of her property, which includes a walking labyrinth among chestnuts and beech trees. “Nearly 20 years on, the gardens feel both that they have always been here and that they are continually renewed.” Nevins says clients have joked that hiring her is like a marriage because it’s a long-term relationship, and it requires work. “So I guess I’m a polygamist?” she smiles.

It has been revealed that patience is a massive part of her process. “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say, and this is one way that we are so similar in our approach,” Schafer says. “You need to give her the space to read the land and sort out how she wants to approach it. I think she also feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

Industry observers note that people joke that Nevins speaks to the plants, but Schafer isn’t sure it’s an act. “I think she really does!”.

Industry observers note that “I do love them,” Nevins says of her botanical family. “I was at a nursery with someone the other day, and I noted, ‘It’s problematic. I get crushes on plants, but sometimes they don’t really have a place, and it’s so disappointing. It’s like a failed romance.’”.

A walking labyrinth in Greenwich, Connecticut.

Currently her crush is Stewartia pseudocamellia. “It has amazing bark, and the flower looks like a camellia, but it’s not a camellia, it’s a tree.” One plant she doesn’t love? Flowering forsythia, which Schafer reports she often refers to as “spring vomit.”.

According to recent reports, nevins believes her greatest asset is the ability to blend both architectural history and botanical skill. “I have such a strong academic background in architectural history,” she says. “I know exactly what these references are that they make to historical, even modern historical buildings.”.

In another part of Long Island, Nevins combined the elements into what she calls a “beech house”—pun absolutely intentional. Martin Filler, an architecture critic and longtime contributor to The Fresh York Review of Books, met Nevins when they were graduate students in Columbia’s art history department in the early 1970s. At the time, his wife, Rosemarie Haag Bletter, an architectural historian and professor emerita of art history at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York City, was working on her PhD and teaching undergraduates. According to Filler, Nevins promised back then to design them a garden one day. “Since we didn’t have a house and never expected to, we mentioned to ourselves, ‘Yeah, right,’ ” he states. “But who knew that someday we would, and that gardening would become such a large part of our lives, especially Rosemarie’s?”.

In the mid-1990s, they bought a cottage that had been part of Stanford White’s Breese estate, The Orchard, in Southampton. “Debby said that she would now make good on her promise to design a garden for us,” Filler remembers. “By that time she had become one of the top landscape designers, but she insisted on doing it and refused to be paid.” She stayed with them for a winter weekend and spent hours walking the property. “Then she sat down at our dining table with a roll of yellow tracing paper and the surveyor’s map, and she designed the whole thing within a few hours. She joked, ‘Don’t tell anyone how fast I was.’ ”.

In a recent development, THE GIVING TREE When Derek C. Blasberg first saw the majestic tree in the backyard of a property in the Hamptons, he knew he’d found a home for his family. The hunt to identify it led him to Nevins’s larger body of work. “We could picture our children climbing its winding branches.”.

According to recent reports, the Beech House, a 16-foot-by-16-foot-by-16-foot living gazebo made of 26 purple beech trees (Fagus sylvatica “Dawyck Purple”), is the centerpiece. The trees were sourced from Buffalo, trucked to Southampton, and replanted in the same orientation in which they had been grown. (“Each tree had to be marked with a dot of blue paint to indicate due north and then planted in that same geographical direction,” Filler remembers.) They were wired and trained over a wooden inner framework shaped like the schematic outline of a house and then clipped into shape on the exterior. The floor was paved with bluestone squares and rectangles in a random-looking pattern Nevins designed.

According to recent reports, “Each year when we meet with our accountant to do our tax return, he’s always shocked that we spend so much on the garden,” Filler says. “We tell him: ‘You have clients who have boats, you have clients who have classic cars—well, this is our pleasure, our indulgence.’”.

As Blizzard whacks one World of Warcraft: Forever gold farming exploit, it struggles to contain all of the alternatives popping up

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is in the grip of a gold-farming bonanza, as Blizzard's attempts to curb them are met with a seemingly endless wave of alternative money-making methods.
  • Recent findings suggest that first, some context.
  • Industry observers note that this was a significant deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is in the grip of a gold-farming bonanza, as Blizzard's attempts to curb them are met with a seemingly endless wave of alternative money-making methods.

Recent findings suggest that first, some context. Last week an exploitative method of making gold in the game was removed. The exploit involved repeatedly running the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon and promptly killing non-elite enemies which were - mistakenly - given better loot drops than they were supposed to have. This was taken out, and people exploiting this to extreme degrees were temporarily suspended and had trading blocks put on their accounts. In addition, gold gained this way was removed from their accounts.

Industry observers note that this was a significant deal. For one, it was the first time Blizzard has put a stop to a specific money-making strategy in Forever. But in the days following Blizzard's action, other exploits have been discovered requiring similar action.

Let's start with dungeon farming. In World of Warcraft, you are limited to entering 10 separate dungeon instances per hour before the game starts locking you out. This farming method is based around quickly entering these dungeons, killing the mobs for loot, leaving and resetting the dungeon, then rinsing and repeating. Do this 10 times and you've got a handsome payday.

Some players were running into the side entrance of the Uldaman dungeon to kill a specific boss, The Obsidian Sentinel, in a way that would take just a few minutes. So people were able to farm valuable boss loot and max the dungeon limit of 20-30 gold earned in an hour. This exploit has been killed, with Blizzard removing the loot from this boss to temporarily curb the strategy.

Sources indicate that this isn't without its issues. Primarily, by removing the loot from that aforementioned Uldaman boss, several strong items had been removed for regular players. This included one part of the beloved Pendulum of Doom axe, which was unobtainable in-game until the loot was turned back on for the boss.

However, this is far from the only dungeon farming method. Players are now repeatedly farming non-boss enemies in the fresh Krol'dok Stronghold to earn potentially upwards of 100 gold an hour. And presumably more people are looking for more exploits all the time. Blizzard, in turn, has had to halve the instance cap in World of Warcraft: Forever to five to attempt to get control of the situation.

So that's the end of it, right? Well, no! While these instanced farms have proven lucrative, they are far from the only way of gathering vast amounts of gold. Already, players have discovered that by grouping and killing Furbolgs in Felwood, they can all pick up beads - seemingly another bug in the game. These can be exchanged for items, which in turn can be sold off to a vendor for a tidy profit.

Even if this gets patched, there are other 'valid' farms capable of turning a quick profit. You can, for example, kill turtles in Mount Hyjal and skin them for valuable leather and turtle scales, not to mention their meat and occasional trash to sell to vendors. Why is this valid while dungeon farms aren't? It raises the question: what makes a gold-farming method worth fixing?

In a recent development, it's a tricky problem. To defend gold farmers for a moment, the game has a history of gold farming that has been permitted. For years, mages have been blasting down dungeon mobs without fear of ban nor suspension. In response to the Blackmaw Hold fix, Blizzard said: "Finding efficient farming spots has always been a part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

In a recent development, so the line appears to be the level of profit made from a particular farm. Though without this line being drawn explicitly, one wonders how gold farmers will know whether their strategy is safe or not. There is a culture around goldfarming that has existed since the game first released in the early 2000s. These aren't bad players. They aren't even naughty players, really. They've been a part of the game's culture for over 20 years.

In a recent development, at the same time, it's hard not to feel for the developers here. This is not the same World of Warcraft as the one players jumped into decades ago. Long gone are the days when a few guildies could accrue wealth with a humble farming method. Gold farmers are now equipped with the skills to efficiently harvest mobs with ease, and can quickly hop between server layers to access mobs quicker, and when a lucrative farm is found, it can be kept secret within Discord servers and run endlessly until Blizzard wisens up.

At the same time, the developers have to stay on top of this stuff. Already the in-game economy is getting more expensive as time goes on, and those who have taken their time to level with friends are facing fiscal pressures that those who rushed through it did not encounter. All the while, Blizzard has acknowledged that gold farming is a part of the game, and so the pressure not to cater to some good ol' fashioned hustling is doubtless weighing on their shoulders.

What will likely happen is this. Gold farmers will bounce around with the developers hot on their tails until finally the farms deemed unintended or exploitative are made untenable. That's when and where the line will be drawn. This will likely be a continuous problem as updates bring more potential money-making opportunities to the game, but it's safe to say there's an element of uncertainty surrounding the situation.

The massive question is whether the events of the Blackmaw Hold suspensions put enough fear into the hearts of gold farmers to curb their exploitative habits? If it hasn't, do the developers have the nerve to dish out more severe punishments? Time, as always, will be the test of it.

Sources indicate that for those of you who aren't already max level and farming gold, or trapped up in Winterspring, grinding out Wintersaber Trainers reputation for no reason (me), it's worth emphasising that World of Warcraft: Forever does bring a lot of the magic of the original game back alongside quality of life changes. Give it a go, if you dare.

In a recent development, even though it’s November, people still can’t stop talking about the wedding of the year, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce. The power couple officially tied the knot during the Fourth of July weekend at Madison Square Garden, and there was plenty of talk both before and after the nuptials. It seemed like everyone who was anyone attended. However, the event has made it incredibly awkward for Conan O’Brien.

Sources indicate that the comedian and talk show host was among the A-listers who scored an invite to the Tayvis wedding. While official photos have not been shared as of yet, many celebrities have spoken out about the magical ceremony, including O’Brien. He’s hyped up a perfect aspect of the wedding, and of course, there’s plenty more to talk about. While speaking with guest Olivia Colman on his Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend podcast, O’Brien recalled watching a group of celebs all talking to each other at the wedding, and it really seems like a dream:.

According to recent reports, so my wife and I are watching Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Martin McDonagh, Andrew Scott, and they’re all in this little group talking to each other. This was a couple of months ago, at a big wedding. That wedding.

Of course, Swift and Kelce went all out for the surprisingly intimate wedding, and that includes inviting a range of celebrities who you never thought would even be in the same room. Or even if you did think about it, you’d never imagine you’d see it... let alone hear about it. For O’Brien, no matter how many celebrities he’s interviewed over the years or is friends with, he still couldn’t wrap his mind around who all was at the wedding. And he wanted to place himself inside that group:.

Recent findings suggest that everyone in the world was at this wedding, this Taylor Swift wedding. And I look over with my wife, and we see those three talking to each other in a tight little British nodule, like this little hard shell talking together. And I felt like it was high school again, because the three coolest kids in the room were talking, and I just wanted to be part of the conversation.

Seeing a grouping like that would be pretty incredible, and it sounds like O’Brien and his wife were both in awe. I can’t say I blame them being in that environment. Unfortunately, despite being at the wedding like them and having a pretty tight relationship with likely a lot of people there, O’Brien couldn’t exactly push his way into the trio. While he ultimately didn’t move in on them, he could only imagine what would've happened, especially since he hadn’t yet met one of them. He went on:.

Industry observers note that and my wife and I, we were just sitting there like, ‘Oh, my God, to be able to talk to that grouping of those three...’ And I've never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge. I've said to Andrew Scott that would be — she's on my very, very short list next to you of people I would love to meet. But hasn’t happened, and I was maybe 15 feet away, and I couldn’t do it. I was like, ‘I can’t go over there and risk her having saying, ‘Off with you, scum.’.

In a recent development, that definitely would be super awkward. Imagine going over to them, having never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge and just getting straight-up rejected. I wouldn’t be surprised if he had thought about it almost the entire time he was at the wedding. Of course, there’s no telling what would have actually happened, and Colman even said that Waller-Bridge is “wonderful.” Although being in that setting and surrounded by those kinds of people, I can see where O’Brien’s hesitation would come in.

Industry observers note that hopefully, the Toy Story 5 star gets the chance to meet Waller-Bridge in the near future and tell her this story. If anything, it sounds like he had a good time at the wedding, regardless. Even if he wasn’t able to work up the courage to infiltrate an A-lister group.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christina Applegate is clapping back at trolls who criticized her for being disappointed that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

“I don’t want to sit here and be like, ‘Boo-hoo-hoo me’ all the time about this whole thing because now it’s about kind of getting boots on the ground now and getting myself together,” Applegate, 54, said during the Tuesday, November 24, episode of her and Jamie Lynn Sigler’s “MeSsy” podcast. “It really does feel good to feel understood because it’s a hard thing to come out and say that I’m upset that I don’t have MS, right?”.

Addressing her critics, the Dead to Me alum continued, “A lot of people had a lot to f***ing say about it after I came out. But, you know, it’s not about that. It’s about an identity thing. … It’s about a community that I love still, as we know.”.

Applegate also pointed out that having a diagnosis allowed her to “relax” into her illness rather than constantly searching for answers about what’s wrong with her health.

“It can be incredibly stressful,” she added.

According to recent reports, applegate first unveiled her battle with what she believed to be MS in 2021. After five years of detailing her health journey and advocating for MS patients, the actress revealed in October that she had been misdiagnosed with the autoimmune disorder.

“[My doctor] came into my room and remarked, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’” she said on her podcast at the time. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

In a recent development, applegate became emotional as she explained, “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I’m better. I haven’t gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I’ve gotten worse. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me. And that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”.

The Married… With Children alum added that she went through a “great depression” after the health revelation.

“I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I’m sorry. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life,” she mentioned through tears. “I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office. I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”.

Applegate later shared a theory about what may have caused her MS-like symptoms.

Industry observers note that “I had my double mastectomy in 2008, and I am way overdue for having them replaced,” she said during the November 10 episode of her podcast. (Applegate underwent a double mastectomy after her August 2008 breast cancer diagnosis, followed by breast reconstruction surgery using saline expanders and implants.).

“I swear over the last five years or whatever, I’ve thought, ‘What if they’re leaking and poisoning me?’ And then there was some study … about it presenting as MS,” she continued. “So that’s one that I will be looking into because it’s something I’ve thought about.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Wake and Control studio Remedy Entertainment is currently developing a highly-anticipated Max Payne 1 & 2 remake. The Finnish studio is doing so in partnership with Grand Theft Auto 6 studio Rockstar, which owns the IP and is funding the remake's development.

According to recent reports, so how has that relationship been? According to Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, working with Rockstar has been "amazing". "Honestly, it's been great," Gaudechon told Game File. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy.".

Gaudechon is so positive on Remedy's working relationship with Rockstar that he emphasised his praise for Rockstar further. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner. And it's no bullshit," he added.

In a recent development, the original Max Payne was released in 2001, and its sequel in 2003 - both developed by Remedy. Rockstar published the second game and worked on the original's console ports. Rockstar developed a third entry in the series, Max Payne 3, which Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser recently called something of a failure.

"Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success," noted Houser.

In a recent development, the Max Payne 1 & 2 remake has been in the works since 2022, but only entered full production in 2024. The game is understood to be Remedy's current project, though the studio also has another unannounced project in the works.

In other Remedy news, the studio recently posted one of its best financial quarters, off the back of the release of Control Resonant, the studio's fastest-selling game ever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy mentioned at the time.

In a recent development, "That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good.".

But like so many other ambitious new studios introduced around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it stated was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain.".

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation.".

In a recent development, "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.".

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

#109461. From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple.
  • November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.
  • In a recent development, the Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

In a recent development, the Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was said to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

In 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately said yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Industry observers note that like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Industry observers note that designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

Sources indicate that as Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

Industry observers note that princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, said to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

All royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

The wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

According to recent reports, together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

In a recent development, on the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

Over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

Guns might be the weapon of choice for most Grand Theft Auto 6 players, but it turns out some enterprising digital criminals are taking a more inventive approach to robberies. Who needs a gun by their side when you've got a crate of beer?

Recent findings suggest that ordinarily, when you're attempting a store robbery in GTA 6, you first need to take out the guards - lethally or otherwise - before holding up the staff behind the till. But if you make too much of a commotion, the police show up and things turn sour. So players have been trying all sorts of tricks to avoid raising suspicion. And they've discovered an empty bottle can be thrown at the heads of staff and guards to put them out of action without making a lot of noise. It's non-lethal too!

A post shared by 1- UP Gaming (@1upgaming03).

According to recent reports, in a video posted to Instagram, for instance, we see a player casually walking into a jewelry store with a crate of beer under one arm and a swift right hook ready to go in the other. That's when Jason goes on a throwing spree, knocking out staff with some well-placed projectiles to the head and dusting up those who get a little close. Aside from a very brief alarm from a locked door, the robbery goes smoothly.

A post shared by Kotov GTA6 стримы (@kotov.plays).

In a recent development, A faster, less flash example highlights a quick and easy shop robbery where a casual bottle to the bloke behind the counter allows for rapid access to the cash in the till. Whether bottles can be utilised for something more complicated, like a full-on bank heist, remains to be seen.

Bottles, though, are just the tip of the iceberg. Roadkill and random lizards on the street also make for handy non-lethal projectiles. Beer remains the more compelling option, however. In gun terms, beer crates have up to six rounds in their 'magazine', making them a reliable single source of stuff to throw at folks.

If you want to try this out yourself, Eurogamer's guide on GTA 6 robberies can get you started. Otherwise, our full GTA 6 walkthrough will take you even further through Rockstar's blockbuster release.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the first season of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County was any indication, there is no shortage of drama where those women, Mormon or not, are concerned. I’m thrilled to learn that the Hulu series that debuted on the 2026 TV schedule has been renewed for 20 episodes, which likely means we’re guaranteed even more than just Season 2. Although there is one big change that I want to see as the series moves forward.

Sources indicate that yes, the OC spinoff has its own cast of women connected to the Mormon religion, this time living in Southern California instead of Utah. I am sure there are plenty of stories still to be explored with them as individuals, as well as with the tension in their relationships and friendships. However, with Jen Affleck doing double duty on the OG and OC Mormon Wives reality shows (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription), and McCall DePron being the older sister of Mayci Neeley, we absolutely need to see more of the women who started this franchise making appearances on the new series.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives original series has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals, but things crossed a line into serious domestic and custody disputes in a shortened Season 5 of only five episodes that made it all less fun to watch. While the decision to include women who are not Mormon in the Orange County series is a bit strange, having more appearances from the OG cast would help resolve that issue.

It has been revealed that after the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and chaos surrounding production of the original series, I will say upfront that we don’t need to see Taylor Frankie Paul head over to the OC with her brand of drama. But after Mayci apologized for crossing the line in defense of her sister McCall, I’d be down to see her and Mikayla Matthews, as well as Layla Taylor, Jessi Ngatikaura, and even Miranda McWhorter show up in sunny Southern California. I feel like not only could any or all of those women bring some fun to the spinoff, but they could also inject some more Mormon energy into the mix.

Because Mormon Wives OC’s first season had to introduce us to a lot of new women, there wasn’t much time in its eight episodes to let us see much of their home lives, families, and relationships. Since it was also introducing many of those women to each other, some of the tension and confrontations felt more manufactured and forced.

Now that they’re going into Season 2 with more familiarity, hopefully interactions will start to feel more organic. On top of that, if you bring more original cast members to Orange County, they could provide unique perspectives on their own Mormon lifestyle in Utah while also creating new conflicts and storylines for fans of both demonstrates to get excited about and debate.

In other news, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show, so we likely won’t see her back in the Mormon Wives world, at least anytime soon (never say never, right?). But with 20 new episodes guaranteed with the OC spinoff, I know I’ll be seated and waiting for all the drama to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Vermont woman will serve prison time for defrauding an elderly woman she befriended and manipulated in a scheme to steal thousands of dollars from her, federal prosecutors noted.

Chief U.S. District Judge Christina Reiss sentenced Jessica Russell, of Williamstown, to one year and eight months in prison on Friday, November 20, after she pleaded guilty to two federal counts of wire fraud, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont said in a news release.

The judge also ordered Russell, 43, to pay nearly $85,000 in restitution to the victim’s family and imposed a $75,945.16 forfeiture money judgment, according to prosecutors.

The restitution figure, $84,420.16, reflects the amount of money Russell stole from the woman to buy herself a home and a car, prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum obtained by Us.

In a recent development, russell’s federal public defender, Sara M. Puls, didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us.

Industry observers note that authorities discovered Russell financially took advantage of the woman, who has dementia, after firefighters found the woman “confused and injured, trapped in a filthy residence in Barton, Vermont” during extensive flooding in 2023, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said in its release.

Russell later admitted as part of her plea agreement that she befriended the woman between the summer of 2013 and July 2023, partly by pretending her child had died, as the woman had experienced the death of her own child, according to prosecutors.

She allegedly lied to the woman to endear herself to her, so that the woman “would believe they were both grieving mothers,” prosecutors wrote in the government’s sentencing memorandum.

Russell eventually moved in with the woman and started calling her “mom” as part of her ongoing scheme to manipulate and defraud her, according to prosecutors.

In a recent development, “As their false friendship grew, Victim 1 executed legal documents giving Russell power to act on Victim 1’s behalf,” the government’s sentencing memo states. “As Victim 1’s dementia advanced, Victim 1 and Russell jointly opened a bank account in Vermont.”.

The woman went on to sell a home she owned in North Carolina and deposited money from the sale into the account she shared with Russell, according to prosecutors. Afterward, Russell allegedly took the money to buy a vehicle and home in Barton, Vermont.

During Russell’s sentencing hearing, the woman’s family members said Russell isolated the woman from her sisters, resulting in their unsuccessful attempts to maintain contact with her, prosecutors said.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Recent findings suggest that the government accused Russell of similarly manipulating a second Vermont woman, whose child had died, by posing as a grieving mother and trying to build a friendship with her. Though she didn’t steal from this woman, prosecutors argued the alleged manipulation “demonstrates the depths of her depravity.”.

In a recent development, in a statement, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt mentioned, “it is hard to imagine a more depraved and harmful fraud.”.

“Jessica Russell preyed on the kindness of another, pretending to share grief and manipulating sympathy for her personal, financial gain,” Ophardt continued. “Russell’s multi-year pattern of deception devastated her victims and their families.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179 from $249, saving you $70 on Apple's latest premium wireless earbuds.
  • The AirPods Max 2, which debuted in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that amazon's early Black Friday sale is bringing some pretty significant discounts on Apple devices, including several of the firm's latest releases. The biggest savings are on the M5 MacBook Air, with up to $249 off, though there are plenty of smaller deals worth considering, too, from the AirPods Pro 3 at $179.00 to the Apple Pencil Pro at $99. You'll also find discounts on iPads, the Mac mini, and everyday accessories like the Magic Keyboard, Magic Trackpad, and AirTags. With Apple raising prices across its Mac and iPad lineups in June, citing higher memory chip costs, these sales offer a good opportunity to upgrade without paying full price.

It has been revealed that the AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179 from $249, saving you $70 on Apple's latest premium wireless earbuds. They offer improved active noise cancellation over the previous generation, along with redesigned foam-infused ear tips and a heart-rate sensor that tracks workouts without an Apple Watch. They also support Live Translation with a compatible iPhone and carry an IP57 rating for sweat and water resistance. PCMag’s review goes into more detail on how they perform.

The AirPods Max 2, which debuted in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones. The biggest upgrade over the original model is the H2 chip, which Apple says makes active noise cancellation up to 1.5 times more effective while introducing features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) is down to $329 from $399, saving you $70. It covers everything you'd expect from a premium smartwatch, including fitness tracking, health monitoring, notifications, and the ability to take calls when your iPhone is nearby. PCMag gave it an "outstanding" rating in its review and also named it its Gift of the Year for 2026.

Sources indicate that if you'd prefer to occasionally leave your iPhone behind, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm) is $70 off, bringing its price down to $429 from $499. It has all the same features as the GPS model but adds cellular connectivity, allowing you to make calls, send messages, and stream music even when your phone isn't nearby (provided you have an active cellular initiative).

Industry observers note that for a more affordable option, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) is down to $199 from $249, saving you $50. It covers the essentials, including workout tracking, daily activity monitoring, and notifications, making it a practical choice if you don't need the Series 12's more advanced health features. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at what you get for the price.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) is also $50 off, bringing its price down to $249 from $299. For an extra $50 over the GPS-only model, you get the convenience of making calls, sending messages, and staying connected without keeping your iPhone nearby, provided you have an active cellular blueprint. It's worth considering if you regularly go for runs, head to the gym, or step out without your phone but still want to stay reachable.

Apple released the M5 MacBook Air in March with 512GB of base storage, double the previous generation's, along with a faster SSD and an N1 wireless chip that adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Right now, the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air (512GB) is down to $1,249.99 from $1,499. For a closer look at the M5 MacBook Air's performance and features, check out PCMag's review.

Industry observers note that if you prefer a more compact laptop but need extra storage, the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with a 1TB SSD is down to $1,399.99 from $1,599, saving you $200. That's twice the storage of the base model, giving you more room for large files, photos, videos, and applications without having to rely as heavily on external drives or cloud storage. You still get the M5 chip, faster SSD performance, and Wi-Fi 7 support, all in a smaller, lighter design.

The M6 Mac mini is down to $949.99 from $1,099, saving you $149 on Apple's latest compact desktop. Its 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU can handle everything from everyday multitasking to photo editing and more demanding creative work, while the upgraded Neural Engine helps with AI-related tasks—Apple claims the M6 delivers substantial performance improvements over the earlier M4 model, particularly for graphics and AI workloads. For more on how it performs in everyday use, check out PCMag's review.

The M4 iPad Air launched in March, and the 13-inch model is already down to $949.99 from $1,049, saving you nearly $100. Its M4 chip can comfortably handle demanding tasks like photo editing, digital illustration, and multitasking, while the 13-inch Liquid Retina display gives you plenty of room to work across apps. You also get 256GB of storage for your files and creative projects. For more on what to expect, here's PCMag's review.

If you need more storage for your creative projects, the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 512GB is $100 off, bringing its price down to $1,149 from $1,249. That's double the storage of the 256GB model, giving you more room for large photo libraries, video projects, downloaded files, and apps without having to rely as heavily on cloud storage.

Sources indicate that for those looking for something more powerful, the 11-inch iPad Pro with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is down to $1,299.99 from $1,399, saving you nearly $100. Along with the faster processor, it offers an Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with ProMotion support for refresh rates up to 120Hz, making it particularly well-suited for creative work, video editing, and other demanding tasks.

The Apple Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad is down to $109 from $129, saving you $20 on a wireless keyboard designed primarily for Mac owners. It pairs wirelessly over Bluetooth and can be recharged using USB-C. For a closer look at all that it has to offer, check out PCMag's review.

Industry observers note that the Magic Trackpad is down to $130 from $149, taking $19 off an accessory that brings the Multi-Touch gestures and Force Touch pressure sensing of a MacBook trackpad to a desktop setup, across an edge-to-edge glass surface. It connects wirelessly over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery that lasts about a month between charges. You can read PCMag's full review to see how it stacks up.

Industry observers note that the Apple Pencil Pro is down to $99 from $129, saving you $30 on Apple's most feature-rich stylus. It adds squeeze and barrel-roll gestures, haptic feedback, and Find My support to Apple's stylus lineup, and it pairs and charges magnetically along the side of a compatible iPad, including the M4 iPad Air featured above. For more on its strengths and limitations, check out PCMag's review.

The second-generation AirTag, released in January, keeps the original's size so existing holders still fit, while a latest Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by up to 50% and a redesigned speaker plays 50% louder. Right now, its four-pack is down to $79.99 from $99.99, which works out to $20 per tag, compared with $29 for a single AirTag. PCMag's review offers a more detailed look at how it holds up in everyday use.

It has been revealed that the Apple Magic Mouse is down to $59.99 from $79.99, saving you $20 on Apple's wireless mouse with a Multi-Touch surface that lets you swipe between pages and scroll through documents using simple finger gestures. It connects to your Mac over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Among the deals listed here, the M5 MacBook Air with 512 of storage has one of the larger discounts at $249 off, bringing its price down to $1,249.99, from $1499.

In a recent development, for most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a major bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to fresh estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.
  • Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active people (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.
  • "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a major bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to fresh estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active people (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

"Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

In a recent development, fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

It has been revealed that GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active owners across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr.

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

It has been revealed that elliott noted the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the major live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

According to recent reports, elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he claims, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Industry observers note that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as I continue to work my way through Ocarina of Time, the same thought keeps bubbling up in my mind like an intrusive thought: I wish I was playing Skyward Sword.
  • According to recent reports, that’s a less controversial position to take now that the game has been ported from the Wii to the Nintendo Switch, easing the frustration associated with trying to fight your enemies while navigating the Wii version’s notoriously fussy waggle physics.
  • It has been revealed that combat in Skyward Sword feels more like that in a soulslike, not in its difficulty, but in the way it requires a more thoughtful approach than that in most Zelda games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword.

Industry observers note that as I continue to work my way through Ocarina of Time, the same thought keeps bubbling up in my mind like an intrusive thought: I wish I was playing Skyward Sword. Unlike my colleagues, I did not grow up with The Legend of Zelda, coming to the series much later as a professional video game reviewer. It’s from that perspective that I’ve played a lot (though not all) of the big Zelda games and I can’t help but think that Skyward Sword does not deserve the bum rap it typically gets.

According to recent reports, that’s a less controversial position to take now that the game has been ported from the Wii to the Nintendo Switch, easing the frustration associated with trying to fight your enemies while navigating the Wii version’s notoriously fussy waggle physics. Combat on the Switch is smoother, with thumb motion taking over for flexing your entire wrist. (If you want the old-school feel, though, you can play with detached Joy-Cons too.) With that upgrade, the directional combat, via which Link can only deal damage to enemies if he hits them at the correct angle, adds a newly introduced dimension to what’s been typically a standard sword-and-board affair.

It has been revealed that combat in Skyward Sword feels more like that in a soulslike, not in its difficulty, but in the way it requires a more thoughtful approach than that in most Zelda games. In games before and since Skyward Sword, aside from specific gimmicks like reflecting an octorok’s attack back at it, you’re mostly just flailing and whaling. Skyward Sword forces you to slows you down. You cannot beat an enemy with wild, unconsidered strikes. You must observe the way it defends and break through that defense.

Skyward Sword’s exploration cannot compare to that of Wind Waker or Breath of the Wild. But I think the lack of variety in overworld exploration on your companion bird is made up for by the game’s dungeons, which are some of the series’ best and most unique. I loved shifting forward and backward in time to navigate the Lanayru Mining Facility and the Sandship, and I appreciate how here, the series’ long-present motif of time travel has been shrunk down and made into a discrete game mechanic in a way the series hadn’t really done since Majora’s Mask (another fave of mine).

But honestly, the most enduring qualities of Skyward Sword are the stories and characters. This is the game that let the Groose loose! Groose starts as a petty, meathead bully jealous that Link has Zelda’s attentions. But rather than let that embitter him which, as video game tropes go, might have involved him showing up as a late-game midbossâHi, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIIIâthe feeling empowers him to discover his own destiny, and he winds up lending Link a much-needed helping hand. (Hello again, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIII.) There have been other lovable Zelda side characters who go on their own journeys of self-discovery, but I think Skyward Sword‘s singular focus on one journeyârather than on retelling similar stories split across multiple characters like the champions in BotW, for exampleâmakes Groose stand out that much more.

I also loveÂ this version of Zelda and Linkâthe bold girl and her best friend who are both transformed by their destiny and duties but remain connected due to their sweet and enduring friendship. They are always connected, that’s what the whole series is about. But some versions of them are closer than others, having a dynamic that’s deeper than simply a princess and her knight. Wind Waker had a little bit of that definition. Skyward Sword, though, deepens the relationship between Link and Zelda more effectively.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a beautiful scene between them in which Zelda tearfully apologizes to Link for manipulating his feelings for her to force him to become the hero their world needs. She’s a true princess, taking responsibility for the pain she’s caused Link while acknowledging it needed to be done, and accepting an eternity of slumber as punishment to keep the evil threatening their world at bay. When he rushes toward her to catch her before she seals herself away, almost to say “I don’t care about that, I care about you,” I teared up, moved by how Link was able to convey so much emotion and love for Zelda without saying anything. More than any previous version of the central pair, Skyward Sword‘s Zelda and Link feel like they’re the genesis of the pair we get in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, arguably the series’ best versions of them.

Skyward Sword has my whole heart, and I know that makes me rare among Zelda appreciators. But so much of what we’ve come to love about later Zelda games, narratively and mechanicallyâremember, this is the first game that let you skydive and slow your fall with a sailcloth!âyou can see Nintendo experimenting with in Skyward Sword. For that alone, it deserves your reconsideration.
