Whenever someone asks him about the upcoming Marvel movie, he just starts playing with the title. It was funny the first time. Now that he's doing it again, I'm beginning to think the MCU's Captain America has found his new catchphrase.

Industry observers note that considering the last couple of weeks Mackie has had, I can't blame him. The actor recently found himself explaining a comment about Paul Bettany that sent Marvel fans into spoiler-detective mode. In a latest interview with Entertainment Tonight, Mackie was asked how the news of Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch returning would affect the Avengers. It's a fair question, and he offered an answer that sounded pretty ominous, even if it didn't exactly tell us what happens:.

Recent findings suggest that well, it’s like, remember you saw ‘X-Men’ and like, Jean Grey, like, blew up the whole planet? Imagine that, but on a different planet. That’s what it’s giving me.

According to recent reports, I don't know that Jean Grey actually destroyed an entire planet in the Fox X-Men movies, but I appreciate the former Falcon’s commitment to making the comparison sound terrifying. And considering Wanda's history in WandaVision and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, I understand why he'd reach for another famously powerful mutant. What he doesn't explain is how Sam Wilson and the other Avengers blueprint to deal with any of it.

The interviewer followed up by asking if he was really claiming he had no idea about Wanda's return. That's when Mackie delivered the line I've now decided needs to be printed on a shirt:.

I had no idea. It’s a lot of Doom in a day… That’s it. That’s my line. It’s a lot of Doom in a day. I mean, I came up with that. I feel like that’s bars.

Industry observers note that this is becoming a pattern. Mackie essentially gave the same answer to gave Josh Horowitz on Happy Sad Confused, describing the movie as a day full of a lot of, shall we say, fucking Doom. Now he's refined the joke into a cleaner line he can use in just about any interview. I hope he keeps going.

It has been revealed that his caution makes sense after the Bettany episode. Mackie previously mentioned seeing the Vision actor while filming, which fueled speculation about an unannounced Doomsday appearance. He later defended his comments on The Tonight Show, as he explained that Bettany had been working on VisionQuest nearby. Of course, that didn't stop fans from analyzing every word. Take a look at this recent interview:.

According to recent reports, I love watching Anthony Mackie navigate all this. With Robert Downey Jr. returning to Marvel as Doctor Doom and so many heroes converging for the next Avengers movie, fans have plenty of questions. Mackie has apparently decided the title will answer most of them.

Derek Hough and wife Hayley Erbert are pulling back the curtain on their relationship — and her near fatal brain bleed — in the new documentary The Symphony of Dance.

The film followed the couple on the final leg of their tour in 2023, when Erbert, 32, experienced a medical emergency.

“At the very beginning of the opening number, there’s a move where she kind of comes down to my arms, I wrap her up and she twists really fast. We both move our head[s] forward and we hit heads very hard. We both kind of [were] looking at each other like, ‘Are you OK?’” Hough, 41, recalled.

Erbert added, “I probably had five dances left, and all of a sudden, I get this excruciating headache, just on the right side. I didn’t know exactly what to do in that moment except for [think], ‘OK, just go back out on stage and just keep pushing through. You’re almost done with the show.’ Derek says I didn’t skip a beat, I didn’t miss a step. I actually don’t remember any of it. And then I came off stage and collapsed.”.

Industry observers note that hough recalled Erbert “dying” on the ground, having seizures. She eventually underwent an emergency craniectomy for a hematoma. Weeks later, Erbert had a second surgery to replace a large portion of her skull that was removed in the initial procedure.

According to recent reports, erbert ultimately returned to the stage just months later. The pair went on to welcome their daughter, Everley, in 2025. The film is dedicated to their daughter.

Hough recalled not being able to keep his eyes off of Erbert when he first watched her perform in a dance studio, but he claimed they “didn’t click straight away.”.

“It wasn’t like this romantic, ‘Wow,’ and then we’re in love. It was just sort of this appreciation from afar,” he explained. “It was a slow burn, where I just was like, ‘Do we like each other? Are we into this?’ ‘Cause she was kinda, like, independent. ‘I’ve got my own thing going on. I’m strong and I’m this.’”.

Erbert went on to note that she felt “intimidated” by Hough considering how well-known he is in the dancing community.

“We took it really slow to get to where we are and I’m really appreciative that we did because we worked through so many things in life that it made us as strong as we are today,” she explained. “And that’s why I think we can go through these crazy roller-coaster of emotions like we have in just the past six months of marriage.”.

In a separate scene from the doc, Hough revealed one of the first things he was attracted to were Erbert’s feet. The pair’s first kiss was on stage, but Erbert and Hough didn’t start dating for months after.

“Our relationship wasn’t usual. It was very on and off for a long time, actually, I feel like. It took us a while for us to really commit to each other on a different level,” he said. “Which is actually what I love about our relationship because it’s gotten better. But it got better because we went through a lot of stuff.”.

Erbert admitted that she’s “constantly conflicted” with sharing details about her personal life while being in the public eye.

“Aside from the fame, there was a weird power dynamic between the two of us,” Erbert said of Hough. “Because we started out as boss and employee. And then of course, there’s the dynamic of, ‘Oh, this is Derek’s girlfriend, Hayley.’ He never made it about that. But, of course, I think about that all the time.”.

Hough went on to note that the pair have experienced “ups and downs” in their relationship.

“The truth is we probably wouldn’t be together now if it wasn’t for her stubbornness, for us as a relationship. We went through so many different peaks and valleys and different ups and downs,” he said, noting that Erbert instilled a “calmness” in his life.

Hough recalled having neighbors who “weren’t great,” sharing that “they pretty much terrorized” his family “in a lot of ways.”.

In a recent development, “They hung me up in a tree by my ankles, like, put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there,” Hough recalled, before seemingly alluding to being sexually abused. “And then one of my neighbors was, for lack of a better word, just really inappropriate with me physically.”.

For Hough, Erbert’s medical emergency brought up complicated feelings toward dance.

“I felt this immense amount of guilt and shame that this happened while she was in my arms,” he stated. “Being a partner not just in life, but a dance partner, I’m there to protect, to make sure that she’s safe. I’m thinking, ‘Did I thrash her too hard? Did I turn her too much?’ I was just ruminating over again in my head. I was like, ‘I did this. I did this. I did this.’ I was just done. I was done with dance at that point. Even a part of me was resentful because I really felt like in that moment, it was dance that caused this. It was dance that almost killed her.”.

It has been revealed that in a separate scene, Erbert reflected on how the male dancer’s biggest priority is “don’t ever drop your partner.” She added, “So he truly felt that he was the reason why this happened. He tortured himself for weeks.”.

While navigating the aftermath of her surgery, Erbert shared that she has questioned why it happened to her.

It has been revealed that “I would go into the sauna and I would just sit there and I would just sob. Those were my moments of, ‘Why did this happen? What is this lesson that I’m supposed to be learning from this?’” Erbert remarked, becoming emotional on camera as Hough hugged her from behind. “I was so scared of losing who I was before.”.

In a separate scene, Erbert shared that her return to the stage was met with “95 percent” support from fans. But there were some critics — including a social media user who speculated that she faked the health battle.

Sources indicate that “One was just like, ‘I’m in the medical field and you should absolutely not be [returning] if this was a real surgery.’ And I was like, ‘You think I faked a surgery? What the heck?’” she mentioned. “Interesting.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Note: This story will discuss a pivotal mission in Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6. A powerful sequence in Grand Theft Auto 6 is promptly becoming a favorite among the game's many players, but a technical mishap made my experience of this scene very different--hilariously different. Chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. It isn't until the mission "Breakfast Run" that Jason is back on his feet, and the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like duo mark his recovery with a crime spree. Set to "Money or Nothing" by Dire Straits, Lucia and Jason rob a diner, not dissimilar to a scene from Pulp Fiction, and a playable montage reveals the pair robbing convenience shops, a clothing store, and other establishments. The image of Jason and Lucia busting open double doors, guns in hand, is probably the most iconic image of GTA 6, a statement of intent that defines the game's story going forward. https://bsky.app/profile/compenderizer.bsky.social/post/3n2yzmpjn6c2j But somehow, I had gotten a slightly different version of this montage. When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut. I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. The problem was that Jason wouldn't put any clothes on. I drove to the diner as the game instructed me to, and the entire mission, Dire Straits and all, resumed with a mostly naked Jason. It was impossible not to cackle at the sheer absurdity of the situation, watching Jason terrorize locals and presumably solidifying a upcoming legacy as the Leonida underwear robber. At one point, the camera cut to Jason's bare foot slamming a gas pedal, and I was left breathless from laughter. Eventually, the game decided to put clothes back on Jason, but I had to visit a salon to grow his hair back. Iconic. Though GTA 6 features nudity in various degrees, you cannot dress Jason and Lucia in their underwear outside of their home. That sprint through the motel room door must have bypassed some sort of clothing check and allowed Jason to freely show skin outside of the motel. I've seen players online talk about an "underwear glitch," and I found one Reddit comment saying that they also had a nearly naked Jason run about in "Breakfast Run," so I appear to be an edge case in experiencing this specific glitch. I can't say that this bug "ruined" one of GTA 6's best missions for me, as I still found myself thoroughly entertained--just not in the way Rockstar Games wanted. Having Jason in his undies while still concealing his identity with a hat and bandana felt like something out of a Saints Row game rather than the fairly serious story GTA 6 was building up to that point. Despite the intense work and detail put into GTA 6, it certainly isn't free of silly glitches and bugs such as this. Luckily, many of them are more amusing than hampering, and Rockstar Games is already putting out post-launch patches for the title. If anything, I'm just bummed that I can't spend the rest of the game as Underwear Jason.

The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut.

In a recent development, I suspected that there was a cutscene that I missed showing Jason fully recovered, so I decided to carry out the mission. Rings Of Power Season 3 Highlights Why Canon Is Not Important In Lord Of The Rings

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article discusses major plot details from "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" up through to Season 3, Episode 6.
  • According to recent reports, as an adaptation, "The Rings of Power" is possibly the most polarizing thing to come out of J.R.R.
  • Now, canon is one of the biggest battlefronts of the internet fandom wars, which (as ridiculous as they are) themselves have only grown as major franchises continue to dominate the entertainment landscape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Keep it secret, keep it safe ... from spoilers. This article discusses major plot details from "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" up through to Season 3, Episode 6.

According to recent reports, as an adaptation, "The Rings of Power" is possibly the most polarizing thing to come out of J.R.R. Tolkien's Legendarium in decades. From characters created specifically for the series to its portrayal of fan-favorites like Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), and its tweaks to Tolkien's Middle-earth lore, the show is full of creative elements that have proven controversial. That hasn't changed over time, either, as "The Rings of Power" Season 3 is now adding a love triangle, a new origin story for the Nazgûl, and a meeting between Sauron (Charlie Vickers) and a Balrog (Simon Pegg) to the pile (via IGN). Suffice it to say, these alternations have angered some fans who feel the series is deviating from the canon and, as such, Tolkien's intent.

Now, canon is one of the biggest battlefronts of the internet fandom wars, which (as ridiculous as they are) themselves have only grown as major franchises continue to dominate the entertainment landscape. As a result, lots of online conversations now center on how, say, a "Star Wars" TV series deviates from books written in the 1990s or how a movie like this year's "Resident Evil" fits into the larger property's timeline. But whenit comes to "The Rings of Power," it's even sillier since the show has to please fans of both Tolkien's books and Peter Jackson's "Lord of the Rings" movies alike (even though Jackson's films themselves make substantial modifications to their source material).

Here's the thing, though: Ultimately, canon is not important, especially when it comes to "Lord of the Rings.".

According to recent reports, middle-earth has a vast and detailed history spanning thousands of years. And yet, J.R.R. Tolkien technically only published two stories in his lifetime: "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings." So, when it comes to the proper "canon" of Middle-earth, that's really all there is to it. Sure, Tolkien's appendices introduce concepts such as the tale of Númenor, for example. But all the First Age stuff like the War of Wrath and the Silmarils, Morgoth and Sauron's history, and the larger saga of Arda all came from, essentially, scribbles and notes by Tolkien that were only published posthumously.

Recent findings suggest that moreover, another thing that makes Middle-earth's mythology so unique is that Tolkien's notes are full of inconsistencies and retcons. Indeed, there are many concerns that Tolkien was able to fully make up his mind about, like the origin of the orcs and whether they are inherently and absolutely evil or not. Likewise, Tolkien struggled with whether to keep his original idea of Middle-earth having been a flat world that eventually turned into a spherical planet (after the fall of Númenor), and he never settled on an answer.

It wasn't just that, either. Much like George Lucas has changed the original "Star Wars" trilogy with every fresh re-release, Tolkien went back and forth on his writing about Middle-earth throughout his lifetime. In the end, he made tons of revisions significant and small to the reprints of his "Lord of the Rings" books.

In a recent development, if J.R.R. Tolkien himself never got around to delivering a complete and finished version of his "canon," then why should fans fight about it? If we should take one thing away from the professor's work, it's that he thought his own fictional universe was malleable, and nothing was set in stone until the last minute. He and George Lucas are far from the only creatives to take this approach, either. For that matter, something as worlds apart as "The Simpsons" is constantly tweaking its own "canon" (with one exception).

Recent findings suggest that this is not to say that we should simply discard everything that has come before and hit the reset button with every new entry in a franchise. Consistency is key, but it's equally vital not to let new ideas be limited by what came before. "The Rings of Power" may be adding things that Tolkien never wrote, but it's giving us Sauron clashing with a Balrog, and isn't that idea just too cool to pass up? More than any other property, "Lord of the Rings" doesn't have an expanded universe that's set in stone, anyway. Rather, it's always morphed to incorporate fresh ideas to some degree, so why stop now?

"The Rings of Power" has many complications, especially when it comes to its pacing. That said, it's always done a good job of reinterpreting its source material in a way that captures the essence of Tolkien's ideals while integrating exciting concepts we haven't seen in this franchise before. Stream in on Prime Video, and see for yourself.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another tech giant is having an outage.
  • Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another tech giant is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication concerns." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Industry observers note that love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering newly introduced security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Sources indicate that mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find latest security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be said for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

Recent findings suggest that you might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October enhancement. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's notable to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

It has been revealed that barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as promptly as possible.

According to recent reports, the implications aren't specific to any one tech giant, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

In a recent development, of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infamous GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek resurfaced last week, threatening to release a crucial file for the Xbox build of GTA 6 that could be used to create an unofficial PC port of the game. The hacker originally promised to publicly drop the .exe file for this version of the game depending on whether their memecoin hit a certain market cap, and has been taunting publisher Take-Two Interactive for failing to prevent the game files from leaking online. "Months of takedowns, subpoenas, and wallet-tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving," Cyberleek wrote in a now-removed post on Reddit, insisting they were "fighting anti-consumerism" in the video games industry with their actions and using crypto funds to work on a new project. "There is no other way to move funds without names," Cyberleek added. "And this work requires no names." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c As pointed out online, Cyberleek has already cashed out on their memecoin in August and again in October, raking in hundreds of thousands of US dollars. So far, it looks like modders are already making modest headway with the full Xbox build of GTA 6, as the Project Leonida Discord server (via Eurogamer) has footage of the game booting up on PC. That's as far as it gets (for now), as that start-up process is met with a black screen shortly afterward. Modders and homebrew enthusiasts are reportedly using Claude AI to reverse-engineer the game on that platform, and the group is confident that a playable build will be ready within a week. Rockstar has yet to officially announce a PC port of GTA 6, but rumors suggest it could be out in early 2027. This would be a very short gap between console and PC releases for a Rockstar-developed game, as the studio's console-first projects usually spend many months in incubation before heading to PC. The threat of a homebrewed PC port, however, could pressure the developer to release GTA 6 on PC sooner rather than later. Meanwhile, GTA 6 has done phenomenally well on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S since it rolled out last week. The game kicked off with 32.5 million copies sold on its first day, and just a few days later, that number reportedly rose to 44.9 million. PS5 sales have dominated, and Sony claims GTA 6 was the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

Ben Stiller And Skyler Gisondo Starred In Night At The Museum Together. Focker In-Law Was A Full-Circle Moment

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in 2014, Skyler Gisondo joined the Night at the Museum franchise to play Ben Stiller’s son, Nick Daley.
  • It has been revealed that as a Meet the Parents and Night at the Museum fan, I couldn’t get enough of this reunion.
  • Industry observers note that it was great.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in 2014, Skyler Gisondo joined the Night at the Museum franchise to play Ben Stiller’s son, Nick Daley. While he’d worked a lot as a kid before that, this role marked a turning point in his career. Now, he’s reteaming with Stiller for Focker In-Law on the 2026 movie schedule, and he’s playing his son…again. So, considering that, I asked the Superman actor how his first time playing Stiller’s kid impacted his work in the Meet the Parents franchise, and he told me why it was a very full-circle experience.

It has been revealed that as a Meet the Parents and Night at the Museum fan, I couldn’t get enough of this reunion. It was also fun to see Stiller and Gisondo reunite now, because I’ve become such a massive fan of the work the Booksmart actor did between Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb and Focker In-Law. So, I asked Gisondo how his history with Stiller played into this experience on Focker In-Law; he remarked:.

Industry observers note that it was great. I mean, Night at the Museum was such a formative experience for me. I was 17. It was my first time being a bigger part of a bigger movie like that. And Ben really took me under his wing then, and was so good to me. And I think I had almost forgotten how much I took from that time.

Again, while Skyler Gisondo was a successful child actor, Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb (which you can watch with a Disney+ subscription) was a turning point for him. It makes sense that he learned a lot from Stiller on it that has impacted his career since.

Industry observers note that speaking of his career, after Night at the Museum, Gisondo booked roles in projects like Vacation, Santa Clarita Diet, Booksmart and more. Also, his last couple of years leading up to his reunion with Stiller have been fantastic. He played the beloved Jimmy Olsen in James Gunn’s Superman, he finished the final season of The Righteous Gemstones, and he was a standout alongside Robert Pattinson in Primetime. Truly, he has become quite the actor, and he’s one of my favorite rising stars.

So, to hear that Stiller impacted him is really sweet. What makes it even sweeter is that while working on Focker In-Law, Gisondo realized all this as he started to notice that some of the things he does as an actor are things Stiller does too:.

According to recent reports, and then getting reunited on this, like 12 years later, there was all these things I would notice Ben doing before takes or something, and realize that I've done that my whole adult life. And I kind of had forgotten where I’d gotten it from or something. And I think it was really helpful for this movie to have that kind of built-in familial sort of relationship.

Industry observers note that knowing about Stiller and Gisondo’s history certainly played into my enjoyment of the movie, especially since the last time I saw them together, Gisondo was a kid. Now, he’s all grown up, and that fact certainly plays into Focker In-Law.

It has been revealed that to that point, in Focker In-Law, we follow Greg Focker (Stiller) as he reunites with his family, including his son Henry (Gisondo). Things get chaotic because Henry brings home his girlfriend, Olivia (Ariana Grande), and he plans to propose to her. After that, we dive into a lot of chaos as Greg butts heads with Henry’s partner, and obviously it leads to some very funny familial hijinks. It’s silly, and it was such a fun way to see the Night at the Museum actors work together again all these years later.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that without the knowledge of their history, their dynamic is funny in Focker In-Law. However, knowing this is the second time they’ve played father and son, and also knowing that Gisondo really had a full-circle moment realizing how much Stiller has impacted him, makes it even better.

So, if you’d like to see this Night at the Museum reunion, and if you’d like to try and clock the ways in which Stiller and Gisondo are similar as actors, you can catch Focker In-Law in theaters on November 25.

As part of its 25th anniversary celebrations, Microsoft also teased a few more details about Project Helix, calling it specifically "a console" that plays games from your PC, not "a PC that can also play console games." This detour is worth it because you'll get cool cosmetics and a powerful shotgun, plus a nice little bump to your health. Here's how you can start this Doom-inspired mission in GTA 6. How to go to Hell in GTA 6 You can find this mission in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County, and it's generally recommended that you tackle it once you've gotten your bearings in Chapter 2 of GTA 6. You can access it with either Jason or Lucia, and you'll need to follow these steps to find it: Start the mission at night, preferably around midnight. Go to the northern section of Port Gellhorn (as indicated on the maps) and look for the Circles of Hell, a house with an open garage. Inside the garage, you'll find two NPCs rocking out. Press L2 to highlight them and start talking. Select the dialogue options "Having fun?" and "It's good" when prompted. Follow the NPCs into a van that appears shortly afterward, and get inside. After being transported to the camping grounds, press L2 to stare into the campfire. Once you've done all that, you'll be taken to Hell, and you'll have to face off against an army of demons. Don't worry! You'll be equipped with a powerful shotgun, so you can mow down the demons and fight your way to Satan. The Prince of Darkness will occasionally summon reinforcements to defend him, but the denizens of hell are no match for a few well-placed shotgun rounds. Finish off the devils, and you'll wake up at the campsite. For your efforts, you'll be rewarded with the following items and upgrades: Circles of Hell top Fresh tattoo design Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun (collect it next to the throne) Permanent health boost For a closer look at GTA 6's supernatural side, check out how to encounter an unkillable NPC, solve the Bigfoot mystery, and help out some friendly aliens.   • It has been revealed that “If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

The blueprint was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is mentioned to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

It has been revealed that “If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

In a recent development, by implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

Ever since the project was first unveiled, "Whalefall" remained a fixture in our most anticipated film of 2026 ... and the movie adaptation most definitely lived up to the hype, at least according to, uh, myself. Who wouldn't be interested in the story of a scuba diver with some serious daddy concerns getting caught up in a life-or-death struggle between a sperm whale and a squid, ending up swallowed whole by the aforementioned whale, and needing to find a way to escape before his oxygen supply runs out? Though the original Daniel Kraus novel was previously considered an unadaptable work, writer/director Brian Duffield found a way, and the results speak for themselves.

Of course, that was the experience of watching "Whalefall" on the big screen. What about at home? Fans who found themselves gasping for breath, shielding their eyes, and otherwise staving off panic attacks in theaters (or was that just me?) can now see if the experience translates to the comforting confines of your own living room. 20th Century Studios has unveiled that "Whalefall" will swim towards a digital PVOD release on December 1, 2026. Those who rent or purchase a digital copy from the online retailer of their choice will also get an exclusive bonus feature (a terrible home media trend we've spoken out on before) in the form of a "Creature Design Audio Commentary" featuring production designer Ramsey Avery and VFX supervisor Guillaume Rocheron.

Fortunately, viewers can look forward to the film's upcoming release on physical media early in the latest year as well.

If you ended up asking yourself "How the heck did they even do that?" every five minutes while watching "Whalefall," we have some excellent news. The ambitious film that once again puts poor Austin Abrams through the wringer after this year's "Resident Evil" won't just be available to watch at home in less time than it takes to be digested by a whale (don't quote me on that fact), it will also come loaded with extras, bonus features, and other goodies for the eager film enthusiast. #109353. The Return of Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow’s Twisted ‘Hunting Wives’ Love Story

The Return of Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow’s Twisted ‘Hunting Wives’ Love Story

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles.
  • It has been revealed that the plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

It has been revealed that the plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

Recent findings suggest that “I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” says showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”.

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.).

It has been revealed that hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter says, “and eventually seduced.”.

Cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she indicates, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”.

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

“The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter says, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”.

In a recent development, the twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a Fresh York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”.

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Industry observers note that cutter says she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain strategy of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”.

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

“Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”.

How To Play GTA 6 On Your PC Or Phone Via Remote Play On Xbox

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox. This means you can play GTA 6 on your PC, smartphone, or a device like Xbox Rog Ally. Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working. From your console, select Settings then Devices & connections then Remote features. From there, check the box for Enable remote features. Xbox Remote Play also has a "test" feature so you can preview the experience in your home environment before going further. From there, you can play GTA 6 from a mobile device by accessing the Xbox Remote Play website, selecting the console you want to connect to, and then the device. To play GTA 6 on your PC or Xbox Rog Ally, owners can open the Xbox app for PC, click on their profile, then select Accessories & Remote Play and then select Remote Play to choose the device to play on. Additionally, people have spotted that GTA 6's store page on the PlayStation Store now mentions that Remote Play is supported and that PlayStation 5 and PlayStation Portal owners can use cloud streaming if they have a Premium membership. Right now, you need a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to stream GTA 6, but some are dreaming of the day when you can simply stream the game to your PC or phone without any expensive hardware. That day may eventually come for GTA 6, as Take-Two's own CEO has remarked the rising cost of gaming hardware is not a good thing and that streaming games could be a massive business very soon. “If you believe in streaming, and to be clear, we really do, and I’m happy to put a timeline on it. I think we’ll be in commercial streaming mode within three years, and by commercial, I mean low latency," Strauss Zelnick said. "That can 10x the effective installed base. Now, it doesn’t mean we’re going to 10x our revenue–and we wouldn’t project that we would–but because obviously your avid consumers already had access to video game machines. But I do think it creates great opportunity for titles that are broadly desirable, even outside of core markets.” GTA 6 is doing just fine without the potential expanded reach of streaming. After all, the game sold 32.5 million copies before launch and generated close to $4 billion in revenue by day one. Even if GTA 6 doesn't add support for full streaming without a console, the game is expected to expand its reach in a major way in 2027 with an expected PC release. Beyond that, GTA 6 is reportedly going to add an online mode in 2027 as well, and it could be bigger than Fortnite.

What Happened To Harrison Ford’s Deckard After Blade Runner 2049? I Asked 2099’s EP For Her Take

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blade Runner 2049, in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece.
  • According to recent reports, deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film.
  • Since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2049, in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece. The Denis Villeneuve-directed sequel not only expertly builds upon Ridley Scott’s 1982 film, but it also adds to the mythology in interesting ways. Additionally, the film includes a stellar performance from Harrison Ford, who reprises his role as Rick Deckard. In the near decade since the film’s release, I’ve been wondering about Deckard’s ultimate fate. So, when CinemaBlend spoke to the creator of Blade Runner 2099, I asked for her take.

According to recent reports, deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film. Found by Replicant Runner K (Ryan Gosling), Deckard is eventually revealed to have fathered a child with his late replicant partner, Rachel. That child is eventually revealed to be replicant-memory-maker Dr. Ana Stelline (Carla Juri), with whom Deckard reunites at the end of the film, thanks to K.

Since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants. Blade Runner 2099 creator/showrunner Silka Luisa is also a major fan of the franchise and, when she was asked for her take on what happened to Ana and Deckard, she shared some surprising comments with CB:.

According to recent reports, I never asked Michael Green, because I'm sure — he was the screenwriter for 2049, and there's just no world [where] he didn't know what happens. But I almost didn't want to know. What I love about Blade Runner is that so much of it can exist in your own mind, and the world feels so rich that it inspires you to create your own stories within it. And something about that period not being totally defined is exciting, because we can all suggest different things. Yeah, so I don't have a definitive answer.

It has been revealed that considering how big a Blade Runner fan Luisa is, I’m honestly shocked over her not asking Michael Green (who shares 2049 writing credits with Hampton Fancher) for a definitive answer on Deckard and Ana. I can, however, also see Luisa’s point, though, as this franchise does leave certain plot threads open-ended, leading to fan speculation. This answer also tracks with the EP’s approach to 2099, which is a standalone piece that doesn’t have direct references to its big-screen predecessors.

While Blade Runner’s ending remains controversial in some circles, the discussions surrounding 2049’s conclusion arguably aren’t as tense. Villeneuve’s film went through different alterations during development, and even the ending changed. Fancher previously disclosed that the original plan was for Deckard to die. While that could’ve been powerful (if crafted effectively), I’m fine with Deckard not biting the massive one, considering it leaves the door open for a direct sequel. And Silka Luisa is down for that as well:.

I really hope they make another. I really hope they make a sequel, just as a fan, to be honest.

For right now, though, fans can return to this dark, futuristic universe by way of 2099. The limited series centers on dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human posing as a Replicant. While fans won’t be getting answers on Deckard, the show covers plenty of ground in other respects. And, who knows, maybe we’ll actually get that 2049 sequel one day.

In a recent development, all episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will begin streaming for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25 amid the 2026 TV schedule. Blade Runner 2049 can also presently be streamed on Prime, and it’s available to watch for free on Tubi.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a newly introduced Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot, Jeff the Land Shark. While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027, priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff below, showing the completed build alongside his box art. See at The Lego Store The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his significant eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail, and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses. For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game. "Jeff brings together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C. Nielsen said in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the unpredictable strategist they meet in battle." Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers: Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies, and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.

Hexed Review: A Safe And Solidly Witchy Disney Original

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1131 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that some of us grew up dreaming of becoming princesses and knights in fairy tales, others of becoming astronauts (or in my case, uh, the guy who gets to drive the garbage truck).
  • Recent findings suggest that the wish-fulfillment of it all probably explains why this makes for such a neat premise in a movie like "Hexed" ...
  • Because being a witch isn't all fun and games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that some of us grew up dreaming of becoming princesses and knights in fairy tales, others of becoming astronauts (or in my case, uh, the guy who gets to drive the garbage truck). Only the coolest — and weirdest — kids among us imagined themselves slapping on some eyeshadow, living it up from atop flying brooms, and casting gnarly spells. Who else but witches can transform the rigidly bland world around us into one positively teeming with magic and color and life?

Recent findings suggest that the wish-fulfillment of it all probably explains why this makes for such a neat premise in a movie like "Hexed" ... even if that potential isn't fully realized. Disney's latest animated original, from directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand and co-director Josie Trinidad, is mostly content to play things safe and deliver a fairly predictable coming-of-age story. While this family-friendly, PG-rated romp doesn't linger too much on the darkness inherent in witches, there's an undeniable undercurrent of something much more provocative at work.

Because being a witch isn't all fun and games. Along with strong personalities and powers beyond compare, they also come with the baggage of being profoundly misunderstood. Their curse is to be loners, outcasts, and pariahs, forever looking for a coven to call their own. Whenever the script by co-writers Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller fully leans into this, embodied by misfit high schooler Billie Doe (voiced by the always-capable Hailee Steinfeld) in search of a deeper sense of belonging, "Hexed" takes on a life of its own. When relying on frenetic pacing and joke-a-minute thrills to sweep us along and glide past any discomfort, it struggles to come together.

There's a greater movie somewhere inside "Hexed," just waiting to break free. Instead, we're left with a safe and solid enough adventure that could've been something more.

Right from the opening exposition dump of "Hexed," we're taken through a prototypical backstory of how witches were chased out of "normal" society and forced to create a mystical refuge of their own called Hexe. Unfortunately, the founding witch died before she could complete this fresh utopia, dooming her followers to wait for the prophesied "Chosen One" to cast a spell known only to themselves and restore everyone's powers to their fullest. ("The foretelling was foretold," as numerous characters amusingly reference this event.).

This intersects neatly with Billie's arc, our rule-breaking teenager with latent witchy powers whose mother Alice (the rather obvious voice-casting of Rashida Jones) has hidden away from the world and from her supposed destiny. When Billie's abilities manifest as an infant and nearly spirit her away to Hexe, Alice takes great pains to hide her daughter's true origins from herself — even to the point of moving out of Salem altogether and into the blandest, most unassuming place on Earth to pass as an unremarkable normie (Ohio). All in all, it's a pretty standard setup for a parable about identity, puberty, and being yourself (alongside a hint of queer subtext), which "Hexed" pulls off with the appropriate amount of emotional, tear-jerker aplomb.

Sources indicate that but otherwise, this is largely an excuse to show off the film's stunning world-building prowess. Yes, Hexe oftentimes tends to resemble Universal's Wizarding World of Harry Potter. But once Billie finally makes it to this living and breathing realm — marked by an expanding aspect ratio to soak in the full scope of Hexe — and assembles unlikely allies like an enchanted pot, Walton Goggins' cat-like and delightfully-named familiar Beef Roger Crummchuk, and neurotic owl Nigel (Henry Winkler), you'll never want to leave this kaleidoscopic wonderland.

Where "Hexed" struggles most, ironically, is in its attempt to carve out a niche for itself amid the vast canon of Disney's animated movies. On one hand, it's strangely fitting for a story about individualism to be so preoccupied by what's come before. On the other, it has the side effect of triggering a tangible identity crisis. At this point, Disney's house-style CG animation has been set in stone and nothing here diverges all that much from the likes of "Frozen" — down to the look of the film's main villain Queen Celeste, brought to life by a scenery-chewing Jodie Foster. Elsewhere, some of the imagery of Hexe itself feel cribbed from classics like "Cinderella" or "Fantasia," coming across less like a loving homage and more like a copy of a copy. Even Kris Bowers' distinctive score is overshadowed by a parade of on-the-nose needle drops, from Queen to Dua Lipa.

This has the cumulative effect of making "Hexed" an oddly meta experience, in a way that both livens things up and makes for a somewhat awkward addition to the Disney pantheon. Much of the humor comes from the script's winking self-awareness and its many "Can you believe this?" visual gags, which could've fell flat on their face but instead (mostly) work. But even its most inspired moments of creativity and imagination feel undercut by a script that's either unwilling or unable to push such boundaries beyond its most surface-level joys.

Still, parents could do far worse than "Hexed" when it comes to movies their children will inevitably re-watch a million times over once it comes to Disney+. While that might seem like damning with faint praise, it does speak to the basics of storytelling that directors Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, and Josie Trinidad manage to get right — especially within a noticeably tight, 103-minute runtime. For all intents and purposes, this breezy storyline might as well be designed to function like a runaway train, constantly keeping the action at a sprinter's pace and hardly giving young viewers a chance to catch their breath. Even the "camera" stays in motion at almost all times and makes the few, much-needed moments of respite and quiet conversation stand out all the more.

This "Get in, get out" approach at least provides a jolt of energy right from the get-go and carries the emotions along with it, even if it can occasionally get exhausting. At its heart, "Hexed" lives or dies by the mother/daughter bond forged between impulsive Billie and overbearing Alice, and its best moments soar as direct result of never losing sight of these two characters.

According to recent reports, there are plenty of narrative holes left oddly unexplained and an unfortunate bit of sequel-bait sweatiness to contend with, likely included in the off-chance this kills it at the box office. (This raises another question, of course: Was holding this Halloween-friendly movie about spooky witches closer to the extended Thanksgiving holiday weekend really worth it?) But thanks to dazzling visuals, a strong emotional undercurrent, and killer world-building, "Hexed" is a solid — if safe — family outing.

"Hexed" opens in theaters on November 25, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two days after a 19-year-old was fatally shot while camping, his politician father is insisting his son’s death “was not a freak hunting accident” but the result of “malicious intent.”.

Escambia County District 4 Commissioner Joe Vinson claimed that his son, Carey Washington Vinson, was inside his tent at a sandbar campground near Blackwater River in Florida on Sunday, November 22, when a bullet fired from outside of the campsite struck his son.

Chief Deputy Randy Tifft of the Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office previously mentioned that Carey, 19, and his friends had been camping in different areas and sandbars since Friday, November 20, according to People. When Carey was shot in the head at 11:30 p.m., a vehicle was reportedly parked on the other side of the river.

Carey’s friends claimed to authorities that they heard the vehicle turn on and start driving after the shots were fired. The friends also remarked they yelled in the direction of the vehicle to make it known that they were in the area.

Tifft added that no one should have been hunting in the area because it was so late at night.

On Tuesday, November 24, Vinson — who was sworn in as the first non-party-affiliated District 4 commissioner in Escambia County’s history on November 17 — issued a statement about the tragedy, saying he needed to “correct a misimpression” that the shooting was an accident.

“This was not a freak hunting accident — not someone firing carelessly in the dark,” he remarked in the statement posted via social media.

Vinson went on to say that he believed the gunfire was deliberately directed at the campsite where his son was.

“As we understand it, some person(s) stood on the opposite bank of the river and pointed a gun at the sandbar campground, knowing it was occupied,” Vinson said. “They were close enough to see the campfire and hear people talking. They fired shot after shot with malicious intent, and after a pause when the panicked campers screamed ‘stop,’ they fired another volley, then laughed as they drove away.”.

Vinson then shared insight into who his son was as a person, saying he went “from a sweet, goofy kid into a sweet, thoughtful young man.”.

“He could play Beethoven on piano and Jeff Buckley on guitar, and he had a beautiful singing voice,” Vinson remarked of his son, who was a student at Florida State University. “He was so outgoing and athletic, playing soccer, hiking mountains, and beating the rest of us to the top of Giotto’s Tower and Mount Fuji.”.

Vinson added that Carey “had a tender and loving heart — for his friends and family, for his girlfriend, for animals, for the marginalized.”.

Industry observers note that “He was quick to laugh and easy to love. I can’t believe I’ll never feel his hugs again, or hear him bickering with his siblings,” he said. “I can’t believe any of this. Every impatient moment, every unkind word, I will gladly take them back if you would just come back to us.”.

Vinson concluded the post by asking those with any information about the case to contact authorities.

“I know it won’t bring back Wash, but I would sleep better knowing they can’t hurt anyone else,” he remarked.

The sheriff’s office has also asked anyone with information about the shooting to call 850-983-1190, Option 1. Those who wish to remain anonymous can contact Santa Rosa Crime Stoppers at 850-437-7867 or submit information through the P3 Tips mobile app.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Inside the NBA’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his aims to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside. The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube) and, when asked about the job, he noted this:.

Industry observers note that I love Charles and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in. The one thing I learned about this business is everything isn't transactional. If Charles Barkley is going to say into a microphone that you're the person that he feels like should replace him, you can't write a check for that. Even if it never happens. And so, for him to say that, it's priceless. I'm so very gracious.

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside, and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal. With that mentioned, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley). Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

Again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

Recent findings suggest that to be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely, he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry.

Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out.

Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move.

You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers.

You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you.

Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off.

Sources indicate that once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work.

If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again.

Colton and Abby got married in June 2025 at The Clubhouse at Talons in Ankeny, Iowa, Abby’s home state.

The couple has been together since at least July 2020, when the football star — who played at the University of West Virginia before being drafted by the 49ers in the 2020 NFL Draft — first popped up on Abby’s social media.

Abby commemorated her husband’s 30th birthday with a celebratory social media post in August.

Recent findings suggest that “Dirty 30!!! Happy Birthday to my guy ❤️ @cmckivitz53 You’re hot & funny,” she wrote via Instagram. “Cant wait to spend the next decade (and life) with you 🎂🎉.”.

As for Colton’s injury, he had the full support of his 49ers teammates in the aftermath.

In a recent development, “He’s somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who indicates up every day with the right attitude,” running back Christian McCaffrey told reporters after the game on Sunday. “He’s the standard, and we’re going to really miss him. We all love him. We’re praying for him. It’s one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we’re going to play for him from here on out.”.
