Sources indicate that before Taylor Sheridan cast Billy Bob Thornton as Tommy Norris in Landman, the pair had worked together on 1883, with Thornton making a brief but memorable appearance as Marshal Jim Courtright in the Yellowstone prequel. It wasn't the first time we'd seen Thornton take on the role of a real-life figure from American history, either, having played Davy Crockett opposite Dennis Quaid's Sam Houston in The Alamo back in 2004. Thornton, whose father was a history teacher, has a particular interest in American history, and for his latest television project, he's going back more than two centuries before the events of 1883.

Thornton's new three-part historical docudrama, Billy Bob Thornton Presents: The Mayflower, officially premiered on Fox Nation on November 23, just in time for Thanksgiving. Thornton, who narrates the series and also serves as an executive producer, told People that much of what he knew about the Mayflower came from what he'd been taught in elementary school, and one of his reasons for making the series was to tell the parts of the story that tend to get left out when we talk about Thanksgiving.

“And anytime you’re doing something like that, you want to tell a real story. You don’t want to just keep on repeating what we’re taught as kids. And there are a lot of triumphs in the story, but it’s also a very dark and painful story to tell.”.

Thornton actually got to board a replica of the Mayflower while making the series, and after seeing the conditions the passengers would've endured on their journey across the Atlantic, he came away with a newfound appreciation for what they endured.

Recent findings suggest that “I was on the replica of this thing, and when I went down into the hole there where the people were sleeping, they literally had to sleep on top of each other. It’s pretty cramped quarters in there with disease and all these things. And by the end of that winter, that first winter, half of them were gone.”.

For those wondering whether Thornton's latest project means we'll be seeing less of Tommy Norris, there's no need to worry. Thornton is already back in Texas working on the third season of Landman, and Sheridan has gone back to his Lioness cast for one of the new additions to the series, with Michael Kelly joining Thornton as the man in charge of the world's largest oil management firm.

The show that claimed the most of your answers is the world you were built for. If two tied, both are shown — you're complicated enough to straddle two Sheridan universes.

Recent findings suggest that you are a Dutton — or you might as well be. You understand that some things are worth protecting at any cost, and that the modern world's indifference to history, to land, to legacy, is not something you're willing to accept quietly. You lead from the front, you carry your family's weight without complaint, and when someone threatens what's yours, you don't escalate — you finish it. You're not cruel. But you are absolute. In Yellowstone's world, that combination of ferocity and loyalty doesn't make you a villain. It makes you the only thing standing between everything that matters and everyone who wants to take it.

Industry observers note that you thrive in the chaos of high-stakes negotiation, where the money is enormous, the margins are thin, and the wrong word in the wrong room can cost everyone everything. You're a fixer — the person called when a situation is already on fire and needs someone with the nerve to walk into it. West Texas oil country rewards exactly what you are: sharp, adaptable, unsentimental, and absolutely clear-eyed about what people want and what they'll do to get it. You're not naive enough to think this world is fair. You're smart enough to be the one deciding who it's fair to.

You are a Dwight Manfredi — someone who has served their time, paid their dues, and arrived somewhere unexpected with nothing but their reputation and their wits. You adapt without losing yourself. You build loyalty through respect rather than fear, though you're not above reminding people that the two aren't mutually exclusive. Tulsa King is for people who are still standing when everyone assumed they'd be finished — who find, in an unfamiliar place, that they're more capable than the world gave them credit for. You don't need a throne. You build one, wherever you happen to land.

That fluency makes you invaluable and it makes you a target. You've made your peace with both. Mayor of Kingstown belongs to people who understand that keeping the peace is not the same as being at peace — and who do the job regardless.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you want to start the Vice City portal event in GTA 6, you must travel to Key Lento, the initial area in the game, and head to the Badger radio tower, northeast of the Nifty Threads Island Wear shop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Vice City portal Easter egg is a unique event in Grand Theft Auto 6 that lets you travel through time. It might not look like it, but the existence of a secret portal in Leonida is quite plausible, considering the UFOs appearing in the skies and the forgotten haunted hotels you can visit.

Industry observers note that to experience this event and open the portal, you will have to complete a long series of steps. But don't worry, below, we explain everything you need to know to complete the Vice City portal Easter egg in GTA 6.

If you want to start the Vice City portal event in GTA 6, you must travel to Key Lento, the initial area in the game, and head to the Badger radio tower, northeast of the Nifty Threads Island Wear shop. Enter the tower and climb to the top to reach what appears to be a control room.

Beside the door, there's a lever. Pull it up then press the button on the panel near the old television. If you've done everything correctly, the TV will turn on and display the word "Malibu." Now, leave the tower and prepare for the next step.

After you have finished the initial ratio tower step, you will need to visit 12 LPL substations around Leonidas following a specific order. There will be a letter or two on the outer wall of each substation, which will form a secret message when all 12 letters are put together. In each one, you will find either a button or a lever that represents a letter or symbol. To ensure you're interacting with the correct one, check the pink tape near the button/lever and look for the letter/symbol it features.

Recent findings suggest that before you start, keep in mind that you can't fast travel using the RydeMe app or swap between characters. Doing so resets the mission, and you will need to return to the radio tower to start it again. You'll know that you have completed this step when you receive a message from an unknown contact after you pull up the last lever. Below, we listed the substations in the order you must visit them, where you will find the button or lever you must activate, and which letter they represent.

Location: Port Gellhorn (Kelly County) — North of Moses' shop.

Location: Hamlet (Vice-Dale County) — East of Massive Shot Ammu-Nation shop​​​​​​​.

Location: Vice City (Vice-Dale County) — Northwest area of Gloriana Key.

If you combine all the letters, you'll get the message: Life is passing me by, which is a PC cheat code that allows you to speed up time in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

The final step in the event requires you to follow the instructions in the message you receive after activating the 12th lever: head to the T. H. Power Station, east of Hamlet in Vice-Dale County, between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m. Once there, you will find the portal that will take you to the original Vice City.

According to recent reports, you can find the portal on the north side of the power station. You'll know you're at the right place if you can see traces of energy from the portal running through the cables in the area. Reaching the portal might be difficult, considering how heavily guarded the area is. Consider either using a helicopter or swimming around the area to find a good entry point.

Industry observers note that once you find the portal, pull the lever on the left side of the gate, and you'll be teleported. To leave the original Vice City, just head to the room behind the bar, and you will be back to the world of GTA 6. By completing this event, you will receive Tony Vercetti's Hawaiian shirt, the American Glory motorcycle (don't forget to register it!), and unlock a new livery for purchase at Vice Vinyl.

WD-40 has been around since the 1950s. While my creaky joints don’t quite go back that far, I clearly remember it being a staple in my dad’s garage. The second anything needed lubricating, out came that familiar can of spray.

Originally invented as a rust-prevention solvent for the aerospace industry, its usefulness has since expanded into the domestic market, making it a well-known household staple. Instead of sitting on your tool shelf, you’re now just as likely to find it lurking in a cleaning cupboard.

Sources indicate that WD-40 is an amazing household cleaning product to keep in your kitchen. When lightly sprayed on a stainless steel surface, like a refrigerator or dishwasher and wiped away with a microfiber cloth, it will remove unsightly fingerprints, smudges and water spots. For this reason, it’s also handy to have in the bathroom to remove water marks off shower screens.

In a recent development, it’s also pretty useful when you’re cleaning your windows, especially when they are covered in bird droppings. What’s more, once the bird poop is dried on, it’s even more difficult to remove, which is when WD-40 works its magic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It only took 24 hours for Avengers: Doomsday to break an all-time Disney record.
  • According to recent reports, ahead of the December 18 release in theaters, the Marvel Cinematic Universe movie is continuing to generate significant anticipation.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to Deadline, Avengers: Doomsday's final trailer is the most-watched in Disney history after receiving 563 million views in just 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It only took 24 hours for Avengers: Doomsday to break an all-time Disney record.

According to recent reports, ahead of the December 18 release in theaters, the Marvel Cinematic Universe movie is continuing to generate significant anticipation. This was only further amplified with the release of the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, which features Cyclops/Scott Summers (James Marsden) shouting, "To me, my X-Men!" as he and his fellow heroes take on Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) and numerous Sentinels.

Recent findings suggest that according to Deadline, Avengers: Doomsday's final trailer is the most-watched in Disney history after receiving 563 million views in just 24 hours. The movie beat its own record held by a previous trailer that landed 503 million views in the same amount of time. Doomsday now also has the second most-viewed trailer in movie history, only behind Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day's 718.6 million, but the record does not solely belong to Disney due to Sony's shared ownership of the web-slinger.

An important distinction is that Doomsday's new look got three times the viewership of Brand New Day's final trailer at 131 million. Final trailers tend to be watched less than their predecessors, as was the case with Brand New Day, which makes the new feat for Doomsday all the more notable.

In other metrics, the final Doomsday trailer had nearly a million mentions on social media in the first 24 hours, ranked as number one, two, and three on YouTube Movie Trending Charts, and got the highest concurrent viewership for the Doomsday Countdown Clock on livestream on YouTube with 306,000 views.

In a recent development, trailer viewership and other online metrics don't always correlate to box office results, but given the massive numbers for Doomsday, setting more than one box office record seems highly likely at this point. The record-breaking trailer definitely ended up correlating with Brand Upcoming Day's box office, which went on to become the highest-grossing movie of 2026 and third highest-grossing of all time at $2.5 billion worldwide, only behind Avengers: Endgame ($2.924 billion) and Avatar ($2.923 billion).

Industry observers note that beyond being the first Avengers movie since 2019's Endgame, the confirmed characters in Avengers: Doomsday have contributed to much of the excitement, from Downey playing the titular villain to Marsden and other actors from Fox's X-Men movies reprising their roles and getting to interact with MCU heroes. Chris Evans is also playing Steve Rogers for the first time since Endgame, and Hailee Steinfeld is confirmed to be back as Kate Bishop after being introduced in Disney+'s Hawkeye five years ago.

Other characters appearing in Avengers: Doomsday include Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), Loki (Tom Hiddleston), Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming), Gambit (Channing Tatum), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Shang-Chi (Simu Liu), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), Shuri (Letitita Wright), M'Baku (Winston Duke), Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn), Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach), Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Alexei Shostakov (David Harbour), Ava Starr (Hannah John-Kamen), John Walker (Wyatt Russell), and Sentry (Lewis Pullman).

Avengers: Doomsday releases in theaters on December 18.

If You Loved 'Phony,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us.
  • Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).
  • Recent findings suggest that A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar reveals) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

Recent findings suggest that A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

Sources indicate that the boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

It has been revealed that the Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a new employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

On one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when highlights are based on true stories, they can unlock something special in the viewer. It can be very moving to know that the actions and people depicted on the screen stem from real events. That's why one of the most powerful shows of all time is still a must-watch. In 2019, Netflix released a four-part miniseries that begs us to look at the racial injustice in this country, and you'll be better off just by watching it.

One of the most shocking crimes to ever capture America's attention was the brutal assault and rape of the Central Park Jogger in Upcoming York City in 1989. The case is dramatized in When They See Us. At that time, the city was appalled by the woman's attack (her identity was initially hidden from the public), and she remarkably made a recovery, even though her injuries were incredibly extensive. The case would have been tragic enough on its own, but there was also a massive injustice that came out of it.

Police questioned five Black and Latino teenagers — Kevin Richardson (Asante Blackk), Antron McCray (Caleel Harris), Yusef Salaam (Ethan Herisse), Raymond Santana (Marquis Rodriguez), and Korey Wise (Jharrel Jerome) — and ended up charging these young men in the attack without any DNA linking them to it.

Four Netflix characters, four completely different ways of showing up for somebody. This is the one who fits how you actually do friendship, and what having them in your life would be like.

You do not do friendship at half volume, and neither does he. What you want is somebody who says yes to the blueprint before you have finished describing the plan.

It has been revealed that you are the friend who makes things happen, and so is she. Together you would be mildly exhausting to everyone around you and completely delighted with yourselves.

You have no patience for pleasant lies, and she has no ability to tell them. What looks like coldness from the outside is the most reliable friendship on this list.

You look after whoever is having the worst day. So does he. It is the least strategic way to move through the world and the best possible quality in a friend.

Sources indicate that the teenagers, now known as the Exonerated Five, were innocent. Through intense interrogations and manipulations, some of the boys were coerced into confessing. These scenes are particularly horrifying to watch because you can see the power that law enforcement (and the prosecutors) had over people of color who already had the deck stacked against them. The youngsters ended up being convicted, and four of them were sent to juvenile detention centers for maximum sentences.

Korey was sentenced to spend his time in an adult prison because of his age, and was the last of the Central Park Five to leave prison in 2002. Their convictions were vacated that year after DNA testing confirmed Matias Reyes’ confession. The Central Park Five were eventually awarded a settlement after suing the city for wrongful conviction. The fallout from the case is portrayed in When They See Us with sensitivity towards the people involved in the real events, and with a depiction of intense themes of racism and the long-lasting effects of trauma.

Sources indicate that the events of the Central Park Five would be intense enough just to hear their stories. But the true pain and loss they lived through is demonstrated onscreen because of the fantastic directing of Ava DuVernay and the impressive performances she was able to capture by every actor in the project. Each of the actors who play the boys absolutely nails both the naivety and the terror they experienced. The true standout of the cast is Jerome, who is able to bring Korey's intellectual disability and kind nature to the screen with a heartbreaking realism. Whether he's expressing confusion in the police station or the anger of an innocent person being accused in the courtroom, Jerome makes you feel the utterly infuriating injustice of Korey's situation. It's no surprise he won an Emmy for this role.

It has been revealed that but it's not just the Central Park Five who turn out astonishing performances. Felicity Huffman plays Linda Fairstein, the head of the Manhattan DA's sex crimes unit, with an icy coldness that perfectly illustrates the inhumanity of the decisions made regarding these boys' lives. Vera Farmiga is also similarly villainous as the lead attorney fighting to put the boys behind bars. There are also several actors who play the boys' parents (including Niecy Nash, Aunjanue Ellis, Marsha Stephanie Blake, John Leguizamo, and the late Michael K. Williams) who are particularly awe-inducing.

Recent findings suggest that they're able to imbue their performances with the heartache and world-weary tone of adults who have already seen so much inequality in their time. Later, we meet the adult versions of the Central Park Five, and this second group of actors is able to seamlessly carry through these roles so that we can see how the trauma has affected these individuals as they've survived into adulthood.

Although many of the scenes are certainly difficult to watch because of the intense emotions they evoke, When They See Us is a masterpiece at depicting a somber true story. It earned 16 Emmy nominations (including many for the cast) and 2 wins. The Central Park Five case is a tale of injustice, but learning more about the story by watching the series is one small way to right these egregious wrongs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Awards season will be making a stop in San Francisco on December 7 for the annual SFFILM Awards Night, honoring four artists who’ve made an impact this year.

It has been revealed that john Turturro, acclaimed this year for his performance in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” will receive the Maria Manetti Shrem Award for Acting, named for the Italian-American philanthropist. (Turturro will also receive IndieWire Honors recognition on December 3.) Carrie Coon, who made a substantial-screen splash this year in “The Liberation,” will receive the Katie & Todd Traina Award for Acting. The SFFILM Award for Virtuosity will go to “La Bola Negra” breakout star and beloved Spanish pop singer Guitarricadelafuente. Finally, the Nion McEvoy & Leslie Berriman Award for Storytelling goes to “I Play Rocky” screenwriter Peter Gamble. Presenters include “La Bola Negra” directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, and “I Play Rocky” star Anthony Ippolito (all of whom are also being feted by IndieWire Honors in December).

SFFILM Awards Night will take place on Monday, December 7, 2026, at San Francisco’s Gateway Pavilion at Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture.

In a recent development, anne Lai, SFFILM’s executive director, noted, “Film has a rare power to change how we see the world. SFFILM exists to celebrate it and to build its future. At Awards Night we do both. We honor artists whose bold, generous storytelling defined this year in cinema, and we raise the resources that power our work all year long, from students in Bay Area classrooms to the filmmakers we fund and mentor. I’m thrilled to welcome our honorees to San Francisco, where the future is always being created, and film is the gateway.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Carrie, Guitarricadelafuente, Peter, and John each bring a distinct sensibility and an uncommon command of their craft to the screen this season,” stated Jessie Fairbanks, SFFILM’s director of programming. “We selected this group because they represent the range of talent and creative perspectives that make cinema so compelling, and their work speaks to the thoughtful, nuanced, and often unexpected films that make a season memorable. They bring a fearlessness, determination, and depth of perspective that we are proud to celebrate at SFFILM.”.

Last year, Benicio Del Toro, Kristen Stewart, Wunmi Mosaku, and Scott Cooper all received SFFILM prizes. The event serves as a fundraising opportunity for the Bay Area nonprofit film organization that also hosts the San Francisco International Film Festival.
